r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding:
Two constraints are not met.

(1) not-a-weaker-guard has a measured counter-case, and the change ships prose asserting the opposite as fact. require_session (checklist_engine.py:1026-1030) returns early when no ACTIVE lease exists, so for a spine with no active lease the lease guards NOTHING and the origin comparison was the sole refusal. Measured by me, same fixture, base engine 9ff86f2d vs the working tree, spine stamped with its own worktree, verbs driven from a foreign git worktree: never-claimed spine, start -> BEFORE exit=1 REFUSED / AFTER exit=0, gate written pending -> in-progress; attach -> BEFORE exit=1 REFUSED / AFTER exit=0. Lease RELEASED then re-driven: start -> BEFORE exit=1 REFUSED / AFTER exit=0, gate written. Active lease held by another session: refused BEFORE and AFTER (the implementer's table is correct for that row only). So the delta is not 'an unclaimed spine can now be claimed from a foreign tree' -- it is every mutating verb, on any spine with no active lease, never-claimed or released, and it WRITES state into a tree the agent is not standing in. Three shipped artifacts now state the falsified claim: docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md 'Removing it removed no guard ... ownership is the lease, and always was'; checklist_engine.py 'Nothing was left unguarded by that removal'; the test module docstring 'Nothing was left unguarded by removing it'. not-a-weaker-guard is @grade settled/human and its own text says a genuine counter-case is a finding, so this is reported for the ruling tier, not decided here.

(2) The Windows case/separator expectation is not constructed, contrary to evidence section 8. Measured: under a stamp-reading mutant, driven from the foreign cwd the test actually uses, EVERY row refuses identically -- the spine's own worktree, the upper-cased copy, C:\W\REPO and a foreign tree all exit=1. Those two rows discriminate nothing the plain foreign-tree row does not. They separate only when driven from the spine's OWN worktree (own=exit 0, wrong case=exit 1), and the test never drives from there. The class as a whole is still non-vacuous, because assertEqual([0,0,0], first['codes']) catches the all-refused collapse -- which is why my mutant went red. Cheap repair: add a third drive, _assert_one_answer_for_every_stamp(self.worktree).

r5-reconciliation.finding:

Doctrine says a settled/human anchor is not the executor's to unsettle and contradicting evidence is a finding to float to the ruling tier -- so the Commander must either (a) get the shipped prose in docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md, checklist_engine.py and the test module docstring narrowed to what is true ('the lease is the guard wherever a lease exists'), or (b) float the contradiction to the Admiral who owns the anchor. It is a prose/scope question, not necessarily a code question: the subtraction may be exactly what was ruled.

Everything else reconciles. The 2026-08-15 worktree-identity ruling supersession is cited plainly in all three required places (docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md:122, checklist_engine.py:96, tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py:22) and the ruling file itself is correctly left unedited. map/INDEX.md moves 1213 -> 1212 script entities and 4737 -> 4699 test entities and regenerates byte-identically. The Map Impact notes match the diff, including the implementer's own correction that the handoff's cited call site :3573-3578 was stale (really :3638-3643) -- the third stale line-number citation this lane has produced.
